frequency_question: How often do federal agencies successfully complete the revocation of an accrediting agency's recognition within a contested statutory review cycle?
membership_rule: Includes all formal Department of Education or equivalent federal agency attempts to terminate the national recognition of a major institutional accreditor since 1990; excludes voluntary relinquishments or minor probation actions that do not reach terminal revocation proceedings.

cases.name: ACICS (Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools) Initial Termination
ACICS Final Revocation under subsequent review

provenance_note: 3 cases named, 4 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.3x)
coverage_note: 4 major contested administrative challenges identified over 35 years; 2 resulted in terminal loss of recognition.
known_gaps: Excludes minor probationary warnings that did not advance to formal termination proceedings.
skeleton: Total formal terminal revocation attempts by the Department of Education against recognized accreditors over a 35-year period, evaluated against administrative survival rates.
multiplier: 2 successful revocations out of roughly 4 major contested challenges = 50% base intervention success rate when political will is applied.
validity_reason: Administrative law standards and the Higher Education Act oversight mechanisms remain stable across presidential administrations, though procedural hurdles change slowly.
